punchline: Michael Gerber has a name for delegating without a system: Management by Abdication.
thirty_sec: Michael Gerber says a business starts in Infancy, when the owner does everything. Then comes Adolescence: the owner hires help and hands over tasks, but with no system for how to do them. Things go wrong, and the owner rushes back in to fix them. His way out is to spend time working on the business, designing how the work gets done, not only working in it.
question: Have you ever handed something off, watched it go wrong, and just taken it back? What would you do differently now?
key_contrast: Doing the work, designing the work
